scope: H0/H1 descriptor latency optimization and proposed 4-CU/16-lane/8-warp host integration. Hardware alignment remains in progress; this is not whole-GPU performance qualification.

change.fetch: Four uncached 64-byte requests use consecutive reserved DMA IDs. All can be live; response ID selects the descriptor line. The 256-byte memory ABI and total ID budget do not change.
change.drain: A fault/cancellation stops new offers, preserves any stalled offer, and drains every issued response before clearing fetching or publishing a result. A late line fault retains command-fault status over cancellation.
change.host: Before shader staging, the reader owns all four host DMA IDs. Legacy DMA and tile owners still serialize. No response can escape into a later owner.
change.width: Use widening addition for base ID plus line index; a nonzero, non-power-of-two-aligned base (3 in eight transactions) catches carry truncation.
change.shader_fixture: Derive vector length and SoA offsets from lanes*warps. Construct large offsets in registers rather than truncating signed addi immediates. Whole-warp fragment batches exercise every shared CU.

functional.counting: 50-check regression contains 47 ABI/legacy/control checks plus three host checks. The final nine-check run repeats those three host checks with active-CU assertions and adds six final-source reader checks: 47+9=56, not 59.
reader_coverage: Full-field decoding, immutable job/result, input mutation and exact 4 GiB bounds.
Allocation and reserved/high-field rejection; healthy reuse.
Four requests accepted before any reply; reordered replies; fault on every line; all live responses drain.
Cancellation before fetch, during a stalled request, with four issued reads, and during a stalled job.
Older fault while next offer is stalled; fault simultaneous with next issue; no new third offer; fault/cancel precedence including last reply.
Response on the request issue cycle, including consecutive issue/response pairs.
Controlled transport windows one and four return identical decoded state.

functional.native_memory: 256-bit AXI; four-bank L2, 8 sets/two ways (test capacity); 4/8-cycle read delays and 17-cycle write acknowledgements. Bare and Sv32 superpage rebinding to +4 MiB.
functional.native_coverage: Each profile repeats all 15 scenario groups from the initial host record, including exact final images/traffic, all fault classes, reset during descriptor fetch, stable result/VM mutation rejection and tile -> strided DMA -> blended LOAD tile publication.

latency.scope: Same final reader with a controlled memory transport allowing either one or four outstanding requests; fixed response latency 12 cycles. Not a native AXI or whole-frame measurement, and not a separately replayed old RTL revision.
latency.bytes: Both fetch four lines (256 descriptor bytes); healthy native jobs still fetch 320 draw-record bytes, read zero old cleared attachments and export 512 attachment bytes only at pass end.

physical_scope: Only TileJobDescriptorReader, default 16-lane/eight-warp shader ABI with IDs derived from four shared CUs (64 transactions, first reserved ID 32). No host/CU/renderer/AXI adapter. TC/SLVT, 1000 ps clock, 25% I/O budget.

limitations: The 8x8 single-tile workload and small test L2 do not establish sustained four-CU scaling, full eight-warp occupancy, target cache capacity or 720p frame rate.
Qualified physical results cover the reader alone. Reported tool area/power do not qualify integrated area or workload energy; no activity annotation was supplied.
One resident tile, one RGBA8-compatible color plane and one D24S8 plane; MRT, two tile engines, broader resources and formats remain pending.
Render-to-texture publication coverage, mixed clear/draw host commands, scoped dependencies, concurrent transfers and driver/Mesa adoption remain required.
Whole-renderer mapping and GPU physical qualification remain open, as do the original H0-H8 gates. No commercial GPU parity claim.
